question: The sides of a triangle are 34 cm, 18 cm and 20 cm. What is the length of its altitude corresponding to the side with the length of 18 cm?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Semi-perimeter (s) = (34 + 18 + 20) ÷ 2 = 36 cm

Area = √(36 × 2 × 18 × 16) = 144 cm²

Altitude to 18 cm base = (2 × Area) ÷ Base

Altitude = (2 × 144) ÷ 18 = 16 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
• 
• 
 C A B H 20 cm 18 cm 34 cm h = ? 

**Given:**

The sides of the triangle are a = 34 cm, b = 18 cm, and c = 20 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Heron's Formula for Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], where semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2

Area of Triangle = 1/2 × base × altitude

**Calculations:**

⇒ Semi-perimeter s = (34 + 18 + 20)/2 = 36

⇒ Area = √[36 × (36−34) × (36−18) × (36−20)]

⇒ = √[36 × 2 × 18 × 16]

⇒ = √20736 = 144

⇒ Area = (1/2) × 18 × h

⇒ 144 = 9h

⇒ h = 16

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron's Formula

Used to easily find the area of a scalene triangle when all three side lengths are explicitly known. Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)].

Area and Altitudes

A triangle has exactly three altitudes. The area of the triangle remains constant regardless of the base chosen: Area = 1/2 × b₁ × h₁ = 1/2 × b₂ × h₂ = 1/2 × b₃ × h₃.

Obtuse Triangle Altitudes

In an obtuse-angled triangle, the altitudes corresponding to the two shorter sides drop outside the main body of the triangle, intersecting the extended base lines.
